+    text = value.strip(_ASCII_WS)
+    if not text:
+        return None
+    if text.isascii() and text.isdigit():
+        return min(float(int(text)), cap)
+    try:
+        when = parsedate_to_datetime(text)
+    except (ValueError, TypeError, IndexError, OverflowError):
+        return None
+    if when is None or when.tzinfo is None or when.utcoffset() is None:
+        return None
+    try:
+        delta = (when - now).total_seconds()
+    except (TypeError, OverflowError):
+        return None
+    if delta <= 0:
+        return 0.0
+    return min(delta, cap)

findings.problem: A very long all-digit Retry-After value (more than sys.int_info.default_max_str_digits, 4300 digits on Python 3.11+) makes int(text) raise ValueError, which is not caught, so the function raises instead of returning None or cap. Malformed/oversized input should never propagate an exception from the digit branch.
findings.evidence: solution.py: `if text.isascii() and text.isdigit(): seconds = int(text)` has no try/except and no length guard. On Python >= 3.11, int('9'*5000) raises `ValueError: Exceeds the limit (4300 digits) for integer string conversion`. Reproduce: retry_delay('9'*5000, datetime.now(timezone.utc)) -> ValueError. Fix: guard with len(text) > 20 -> return cap, or wrap int() in try/except ValueError.
